quote: we can get you, talking to a specialist to show what we can offer you. Okay?
stewart_read: Customer opens by asking for an estimate; rep immediately redirects to the specialist rather than attempting to quote or explain pricing himself. This is the universal escape hatch executed correctly, right at the top of the call.
coaching_implication: Reinforce this as the model move — rep should keep doing this reflexively whenever a customer asks for numbers up front.

quote: do you have a credit score over 6 70?
stewart_read: Rep states the 670 threshold exactly matching the schema, notable given other calls in the corpus show drift (e.g., 650 stated elsewhere). Clean, correct qualifier delivery.
coaching_implication: No coaching needed here — worth naming in the 1-on-1 as a positive baseline the rep is already hitting.

quote: I have metal. One part of newer. One part, a 100 years old.
stewart_read: Customer volunteers a striking detail — part of the roof is a century old — which borders on a hard DQ condition (roof age) and also a potential cross-sell signal (roof replacement) if that section needs work. Rep logs it and moves straight to the credit question without probing either angle.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive read: rep simply didn't register the number as unusual and moved on out of habit. Strategic read would require evidence the rep deferred this deliberately to the specialist, which isn't present here — the rep gives no bridging line at all.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to flag unusual roof-age answers for a quick follow-up question (age of the older section, any replacement plans) — this is free diagnostic and cross-sell value being left on the table.

quote: Are you just are you able to access the power bill real quick? We say one thing.
stewart_read: Rep asks for bill access without first checking who controls the account, then commits to the photo-text plan even after learning the wife manages the app electronically. The friction stretches roughly three minutes before resolving.
alternative_hypothesis: Strategic read: rep may have judged that waiting for the wife to navigate the app was still faster than a verbal read-back given the customer wasn't holding the bill himself either. There's no direct evidence the rep considered pivoting, so this reads as reactive persistence rather than a deliberate choice.
coaching_implication: When a third party ends up controlling bill access, the rep should check in around the 2-minute mark and offer a fallback (verbal numbers, or defer bill capture to the specialist) rather than riding out the full exchange silently.

quote: It doesn't give her a total cable offer to you.
stewart_read: This is the second touch of the same bill-access friction — the rep is still working through a confusing, garbled exchange about what the app displays, roughly two minutes after the first friction point. No pivot to a verbal read-back has occurred yet.
alternative_hypothesis: Strategic read: the rep may have been intentionally patient because the customer's wife was already mid-task and abandoning the photo path risked losing the momentum. This is plausible but unconfirmed — the rep gives no verbal indication of a considered trade-off.
coaching_implication: Second touch of the same friction point without a pivot suggests the rep needs a clearer internal trigger for 'this has gone past two minutes, offer the fallback' rather than waiting for the customer to sort it out.

stewart_read: Rep texts a photo request to a number in the exchange; it's unclear from the transcript whether this is the rep's personal line or a company line — the schema's personal-phone-number detection signal requires explicit framing like 'from my personal line,' which is not present here.
alternative_hypothesis: This could be a routine business SMS number rather than a personal-phone privacy exposure; the transcript doesn't resolve it either way.
coaching_implication: Worth a quick factual check with the rep on what number is used for these texts — not flagged as a violation, just an open question for the manager to confirm the floor's texting setup.

quote: Can you do a phone call appointment tomorrow?
stewart_read: Rep moves cleanly into scheduling once the bill photo lands, and works through two time offers before landing on 3PM — a workable, if minimal, booking close.
coaching_implication: The scheduling exchange itself is fine, but the rep skips the fuller button-up elements (hour block, no-driving/computer instruction, 'is that fair' handshake) — worth flagging separately as a process gap even though a time was locked.
